models._description: Adds totp_secret, totp_last_counter, totp_enabled, totp_trusted_device_ids + MFA hooks

behavioral_notes.observation: Enrolment is a self-service, identity-checked flow. action_totp_enable_wizard (guarded by @check_identity and a 'yourself only' UserError) mints a fresh 160-bit secret with os.urandom(TOTP_SECRET_SIZE//8), base32-encodes it, and spawns the auth_totp.wizard. The wizard's _compute_qrcode builds an 'otpauth://totp/{issuer}:{login}?secret=..&algorithm=SHA1&digits=6&period=30' URI and renders it to a PNG QR via the qrcode lib for scanning by Google Authenticator/Authy. wizard.enable() -> res.users._totp_try_setting(secret, code): it refuses if totp_enabled already or self != env.user, verifies the typed code against the secret with TOTP(...).match, and only on success writes totp_secret (groups=NO_ACCESS, stored via raw _inverse_token UPDATE bypassing ORM cache) and seeds totp_last_counter. It then recomputes the session token (_compute_session_token) so the secret-change cache clear does not log the user out. Secret is wiped from the transient wizard post-enable.

The login 2FA gate. After password auth, _mfa_type() returns 'totp' when totp_enabled and _mfa_url() returns '/web/login/totp', so web's login flow holds the user at pre_uid (not yet a full session) and redirects to the TOTP form instead of finalizing. controllers/home.web_totp POSTs the code into res.users._check_credentials({'type':'totp','token':int(code)}, ...): it b32decodes totp_secret and calls TOTP(key).match(token); a miss raises AccessDenied('Verification failed, please double-check the 6-digit code'); a replay (match <= totp_last_counter) raises AccessDenied('please use the latest 6-digit code'). Only on success is totp_last_counter advanced and request.session.finalize(env) called to elevate pre_uid into an authenticated session. The whole exchange is wrapped in user._assert_can_auth and _totp_rate_limit('code_check') caps it at 5 verifications/hour/user (purged on success); a sibling 'send_email' limit (5/hr) exists for the email-OTP variant. Enabling TOTP also flips _rpc_api_keys_only() True, forbidding password-based RPC.

auth_totp.device inherits res.users.apikeys (_auto=False, secret 'key' column) to reuse the hashed-secret machinery for 'remember this device'. On a successful TOTP login with remember=1, controllers/home calls auth_totp.device.sudo()._generate('browser', name, expiry): it generates a 20-byte os.urandom hex token, stores only KEY_CRYPT_CONTEXT.hash(token) (pbkdf2_sha512, 6000 rounds) plus an 8-hex-digit index, and the *plaintext* token is set as the httponly, SameSite=Lax 'td_id' cookie (max_age = auth_totp.trusted_device_age ICP, default 90 days; device named '<browser> on <platform> (<city>, <country>)' via GeoIP). On a later GET the cookie is verified by _check_credentials_for_uid(scope='browser', key, uid) -> _check_apikey_credentials, which looks up by index then does a timing-safe KEY_CRYPT_CONTEXT.verify(key, stored_hash) (passlib's constant-time compare, the consteq equivalent) and, only on a uid match, request.session.finalize() skips the TOTP prompt entirely. Devices are revoked on TOTP disable, on change_password (_revoke_all_devices), and via revoke_all_devices().

TOTP is implemented in-tree from stdlib (no pyotp dependency). hotp(secret, counter) packs the counter big-endian (struct '>Q'), computes hmac.new(secret, C, sha1).digest(), takes the RFC 4226 dynamic-truncation offset from the last nibble, reads a 31-bit big-endian int and mods 10**6 -> a 6-digit code. TOTP.match() turns wall-clock time into counters with a +/-30s fuzz window (TIMESTEP=30) and returns the matching counter (used as totp_last_counter to block replay) or None. Parameters are fixed (sha1 / 6 digits / 30s) for Google Authenticator compatibility. This pure-crypto core is wholly invisible to ORM/AST metadata.

No OWL components, JS modules, registry adds, services or patches: the only client footprint is static/src/scss/res_users_view_form.scss (one rule, .o_auth_2fa_btn font-size) plus QWeb login templates (views/templates.xml: auth_totp.auth_totp_form) and JS browser tests (static/tests/totp_flow.js, apikeys_flow.js). Asset bundles touched: web.assets_backend (1, the scss) and web.assets_tests (1). The 2FA enable/disable UI is server-rendered form views + a wizard dialog, not a custom OWL component.

it_architecture.application: auth_totp (Two-Factor Authentication via TOTP: authenticator-app second factor + trusted-device opt-out, layered on the web login flow)
software_services: /web/login/totp (public HTTP: TOTP challenge form GET/POST, trusted-device cookie check)
information_flows: depends: web (extends web's login controller + res.users auth hooks)
enrol: action_totp_enable_wizard -> auth_totp.wizard (otpauth QR) -> _totp_try_setting -> res.users.totp_secret (+ session token refresh)
challenge: web login -> _mfa_type/_mfa_url='/web/login/totp' -> home.web_totp -> res.users._check_credentials(type=totp) -> TOTP.match -> session.finalize | AccessDenied
trust: web_totp(remember) -> auth_totp.device._generate('browser') -> httponly 'td_id' cookie -> later GET verify via _check_apikey_credentials -> skip prompt
side-effect: totp_enabled=True -> _rpc_api_keys_only()=True (password RPC disabled, API keys required)

capabilities: TOTP Secret Enrolment & Provisioning (QR / otpauth URI)
value_streams: Enrol-to-Protected: enable wizard -> scan QR -> verify code -> account hardened with second factor
Login-to-Session: password -> TOTP challenge -> code/trusted-cookie verify -> finalized authenticated session
policies: 4 record rules: users see/manage only their own trusted devices/wizard ([('user_id','=',user.id)]); public users blocked from devices ([(0,'=',1)]); administrators (base.group_system) may view devices to revoke
Rate-limit policy: 5 code verifications/hour and 5 auth-mails/hour per user (TOTP_RATE_LIMITS), AccessDenied on breach
Replay policy: each accepted counter must exceed totp_last_counter (one-time use per 30s step)
Disable action restricted to self or base.group_erp_manager / system; 2FA forces API-key-only RPC
stakeholders: End user / employee (enrols and authenticates with a second factor)
Portal user (read access to own trusted devices)
Security administrator / ERP manager (enforces and revokes 2FA, audits rate-limit logs)
metrics: auth.totp.rate.limit.log rows per user/IP (failed-attempt / abuse signal)
_logger 2FA audit events (enable/disable/check SUCCESS|FAIL|REUSE|REJECT) for the security log trail
count of users with totp_enabled (2FA adoption / coverage)

classification.rationale: auth_totp is IT security infrastructure (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It hardens identity & access and owns no business object of its own: its three tiny models are a transient enrolment wizard, a hashed trusted-device token (reusing res.users.apikeys), and a rate-limit ledger — it exists solely to add a second authentication factor to the web login that EVERY other module sits behind (auth_install=true, depends only on web). It creates no document chain, holds no customer/order/product/ledger data, and produces no primary-activity output, so it is classified 'support' rather than chain/shop/network. APQC 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' is the precise fit: this is the 'manage IT security, privacy and data protection' / 'identity & access management' capability — a concrete running access-control runtime (TOTP/HOTP crypto, MFA challenge controller, trusted-device cookies, brute-force throttling). 11.0 'Manage Enterprise Risk, Compliance, Remediation and Resiliency' was considered because 2FA mitigates account-takeover risk and supports compliance mandates, but rejected: 11.0 covers the governance layer (risk registers, control frameworks, audits, policy management), whereas auth_totp is the technical *implementation* of an access control that IT operates and delivers — the build/run of a security mechanism, which APQC places under 8.0 (Develop and manage IT security, privacy and data protection / Manage IT security). The classification mirrors the sibling auth_* identity modules and the web framework record (both 8.0/support).

standard_capabilities: TOTP (RFC 6238) authenticator-app second factor, in-tree HOTP/SHA1/6-digit/30s, Google Authenticator-compatible otpauth QR enrolment
Login MFA challenge wired into the web login flow via _mfa_type/_mfa_url and a public /web/login/totp controller
Replay protection (monotonic totp_last_counter) and +/-30s clock-skew window
Trusted-device 'remember this browser' via httponly SameSite=Lax cookie backed by a hashed (pbkdf2_sha512) token, default 90-day expiry (auth_totp.trusted_device_age ICP)
Per-user/IP rate limiting (5 code checks/hr, 5 auth mails/hr) with an auditable log
Self-service enable/disable plus administrator revocation (group_erp_manager/system) and revoke-all-devices
Auto-forces API-key-only RPC once 2FA is enabled (no password RPC)
Full security audit logging of enable/disable/check outcomes
typical_fits: Mandating 2FA for sensitive/admin users out of the box (no custom code)
Letting users self-enrol with any standard authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password, FreeOTP)
Reducing prompt fatigue with trusted-device opt-out on personal browsers
Tuning trusted-device lifetime via the auth_totp.trusted_device_age system parameter
common_gaps: No org-wide enforcement policy / 'require 2FA for group X' toggle out of the box (needs config or auth_totp_mail-style add-on)
Email-OTP delivery is provided by the separate auth_totp_mail module, not this base module
Fixed algorithm (SHA1/6/30) — no UI to change digits/period/hash
No SMS or hardware-token (WebAuthn/passkey) factor here — separate auth_passkey module
No self-service recovery/backup-codes flow (admin disable is the reset path)
drive_hints: odoo shell: u = env['res.users'].browse(2); u._mfa_type(); u.totp_enabled  # inspect a user's 2FA state
odoo shell: from odoo.addons.auth_totp.models.totp import TOTP; import base64,time; TOTP(base64.b32decode(secret)).match(code)  # verify a code against a secret
odoo shell: env['auth.totp.rate.limit.log'].search_read([], ['user_id','ip','limit_type','create_date'], limit=5)  # inspect throttle ledger
curl -i 'http://localhost:8069/web/login/totp'  # without a pre_uid session it 303-redirects to /web/login (proves the gate)
odoo shell: env['res.users'].browse(2).totp_trusted_device_ids.mapped('name')  # list a user's trusted devices
